Local command and composer ownership reviewed. The executable comparison covers only completed-tool selection and queued-message eligibility. Full turn execution, Stop races, payload recovery, provider delivery and browser behavior remain unverified.

localMapping.owner: Chat session composer owns queued intent; client-core builds commands; server orchestration owns accepted turns.
localMapping.capability: Interrupt a running turn and recover unsent queued follow-ups.
localMapping.defaults: chat.followUpBehavior defaults to queue and can select steer; the alternate shortcut inverts it. Held messages require explicit action; connecting blocks automatic send.
localMapping.results: The composer drains queued intent before dispatching session.turn.interrupt and then settles the session projection.
localMapping.navigation: The same scoped environment/session owns its draft and queue. Queue policy does not change the active session.
localMapping.persistence: Queued intents are in memory. Stop restores never-submitted draft content; unknown-outcome submissions stay held with their original command IDs for deduplicated retry. Full attachment persistence, reload and cross-client behavior require separate runtime acceptance.
localMapping.negativePaths: The paired corpus rejects connecting sends, automatic held sends, repeated same-tool sends, positional tool ordering and timestamp-first ordering. Provider errors, interruption races and complete command failures remain unverified.
